imperative:anta.why: The generator skips this hamzated verb, so the table holds only the Uthmani سْـَٔلِ (12:82). اِسْأَلْ is the standard full imperative and سَلْ the classical short one (cf. 2:211 سَلْ).

The hollow imperative زِدْ (20:114 رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا) is too short for the analyzer to read, so no analyzable spelling exists; this records it as the documented standard form the gate confirms by the table.

past:huwa.why: عَسَى is an inflexible (jāmid) verb the analyzer reads only as a noun, and the table holds only the Uthmani عَسَىٰٓ (27:72) with its dagger alif. عَسَى is the standard spelling; this records it so the gate confirms the verb by the table.

imperative:anta.why: The hamzated imperative of أَذِنَ is attested only as Uthmani ٱئْذَن (9:49 ٱئْذَن لِّى), which the analyzer cannot read, nor any plain spelling of it. اِئْذَنْ (hamzat al-wasl, then the radical hamza on a yāʾ seat) is the standard imlāʾī form; this records it so the gate confirms it by the table.

imperative:antum.why: The only attested plural imperative is فَأْذَنُوا۟ (2:279), where the hamzat al-wasl drops after fa; the standalone standard form اِئْذَنُوا is not readable by the analyzer. This records it so a sentence can open with the verb and the gate confirms it by the table.

The generator skips this hamzated verb, so the table holds only the Uthmani ٱقْرَءُوا۟ (69:19 هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ), whose hamza on the line the gate does not match against the standard spelling. اِقْرَؤُوا (hamza on wāw before the plural ending) is the standard form; this records it so the gate confirms it by the table and the table shows it.
